_readme: Presentation-layer lookup: one 15–30-word intro per institution — what the firm is and whom it manages money for — shown under the name in the drill-down. Drafted from general knowledge and each row's own type/region/AUM fields, not from the evidence record; it introduces the firm, never the AI claim, and carries no facts the stage rests on. `basis` records how each line was produced; `source_url` is the firm homepage from homepages.json where one exists, else null. Never modifies institutions.json.

CalSTRS.text: The second-largest US public pension fund, managing retirement benefits for California's public-school educators; invests globally across public and private markets.

CalPERS.text: The largest US public pension fund, administering retirement and health benefits for California state, school and public-agency employees and retirees; based in Sacramento.

NBIM (Norges Bank Investment Management).text: Asset-management arm of Norway's central bank; manages the Government Pension Fund Global, the world's largest sovereign wealth fund, built from the country's petroleum revenues.

CPP Investments.text: Toronto-based Crown corporation that invests the assets of the Canada Pension Plan, at arm's length from government, on behalf of Canadian contributors and beneficiaries.

GIC.text: Sovereign wealth fund wholly owned by the Government of Singapore; manages the country's foreign reserves for the long term across public and private markets worldwide.

BlackRock.text: New York-listed asset manager, the world's largest, running iShares index funds alongside active and alternative strategies for institutions and individuals; also licenses its Aladdin risk platform.

Temasek.text: Investment company owned by the Government of Singapore that holds and manages a global portfolio of equity stakes, including in many of Singapore's largest companies.

Vanguard.text: Pennsylvania-based mutual-fund and ETF manager owned by its own US funds, and thus by their investors; built around low-cost index investing for individuals and institutions.

Bridgewater Associates.text: Connecticut-based hedge fund founded by Ray Dalio, running systematic global-macro strategies such as Pure Alpha and All Weather for institutional clients.

Man Group.text: London-listed alternative investment manager, among the largest publicly traded hedge-fund firms, running systematic (Man AHL, Man Numeric) and discretionary strategies for institutional clients worldwide.

AQR Capital Management.text: Greenwich, Connecticut-based quantitative investment manager co-founded by Cliff Asness; runs systematic, factor-based strategies across asset classes for institutional clients and in mutual funds.

Schroders.text: London-listed asset manager with the founding Schroder family still its largest shareholder; runs active public-market, private-market (Schroders Capital) and wealth-management businesses for institutions and individuals worldwide.

T. Rowe Price.text: Baltimore-based, publicly listed asset manager focused on actively managed mutual funds and retirement-plan services for individual investors, financial intermediaries and institutions worldwide.

Balyasny Asset Management.text: Chicago-founded multi-strategy hedge fund led by founder Dmitry Balyasny, allocating capital across many independent portfolio-manager teams in equities, macro, credit and other strategies.

MacArthur Foundation.text: Chicago-based private philanthropic foundation, endowed from the estate of insurance entrepreneur John D. MacArthur, that makes grants and impact investments worldwide; best known for the MacArthur Fellows.

PGGM.text: Dutch pension administrator and asset manager, based in Zeist, that invests primarily for PFZW, the pension fund for the Netherlands' healthcare and social-work sector.

OMERS.text: Toronto-based defined-benefit pension plan for Ontario's municipal-sector employees, including police, firefighters and paramedics; invests across public and private markets through in-house teams.

BCI (British Columbia Investment Managem.text: Crown corporation based in Victoria, British Columbia, that invests on behalf of the province's public-sector pension plans, insurance funds and other public bodies across public and private markets.

HOOPP (Healthcare of Ontario Pension Pla.text: Toronto-based defined-benefit pension plan for Ontario's hospital and healthcare workers, jointly governed by the Ontario Hospital Association and healthcare unions; manages most of its assets in-house.

National Pension Service (NPS).text: South Korea's state-run national pension fund, operating under the Ministry of Health and Welfare and covering most of the country's workforce; its investment office is based in Jeonju.

ATP (Arbejdsmarkedets Tillægspension).text: Denmark's statutory supplementary labour-market pension, covering nearly all Danish workers through mandatory contributions; an independent institution based in Hillerød that also administers public benefits.

MassPRIM (Massachusetts Pension Reserves.text: Massachusetts state board that invests the Pension Reserves Investment Trust (PRIT) Fund, pooling the pension assets of the state's employees, teachers and participating local retirement systems.

Franklin Templeton.text: San Mateo, California-based, publicly listed asset manager (Franklin Resources) offering active funds, ETFs and alternatives through specialist affiliates such as Western Asset, ClearBridge and Putnam.

EQT.text: Stockholm-listed private-markets investment firm founded with backing from the Wallenberg family's Investor AB; runs private equity, infrastructure and real-estate funds for institutional investors worldwide.

Amundi.text: Paris-listed asset manager, majority-owned by Crédit Agricole and Europe's largest, running active, passive and alternative funds for partner retail banks and institutional clients worldwide.

Citadel.text: Miami-headquartered multi-strategy hedge fund founded by Ken Griffin, trading equities, fixed income and macro, commodities, credit and quantitative strategies; distinct from the market maker Citadel Securities.

Two Sigma.text: New York-based quantitative hedge fund founded by John Overdeck and David Siegel, running systematic, model-driven strategies across global markets for institutional investors.

CSOP Asset Management.text: Hong Kong-based subsidiary of China Southern Asset Management, the first offshore arm set up by a mainland Chinese fund house; specializes in ETFs on Chinese and Asian markets.

State Street Investment Management (SSGA.text: Boston-based asset-management arm of State Street Corporation, the custody bank; runs the SPDR ETF family and index and active mandates for institutional and intermediary clients worldwide.

Millennium Management.text: New York-based multi-strategy hedge fund founded by Israel Englander, allocating capital to hundreds of independent trading teams across equities, fixed income, commodities and quantitative strategies.

Fidelity Investments.text: Boston-based, privately held financial-services group controlled by the Johnson family; runs mutual funds and manages retirement plans, brokerage and custody for individuals, employers and institutions.

PGIM.text: Newark, New Jersey-based asset-management business of the insurer Prudential Financial; runs fixed-income, equity, real-estate and private-credit strategies for institutional and retail clients worldwide through specialist affiliates.

Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB).text: Malaysian state-linked fund manager, established to broaden Bumiputera share ownership, that runs unit trusts for millions of Malaysian retail investors through its ASNB arm; based in Kuala Lumpur.

M&G.text: London-listed savings and investment group, demerged from Prudential plc, that combines the asset manager M&G Investments with a UK life-insurance and with-profits business serving retail and institutional clients.

AllianceBernstein.text: Nashville-headquartered, publicly traded asset manager majority-owned by the insurer Equitable Holdings; runs active equity, fixed-income and alternative strategies alongside the Bernstein private-wealth business.

Ares Management.text: Los Angeles-based, publicly listed alternative asset manager with private credit its largest business, alongside private equity, real assets and secondaries; invests for institutional and wealth clients worldwide.

Aberdeen Group (abrdn).text: Edinburgh-based listed investment group, formed by merging Standard Life and Aberdeen Asset Management, that combines an asset manager with a UK adviser platform and the interactive investor retail platform.

Legal & General.text: London-listed insurance and asset-management group whose asset-management arm (LGIM) runs index, fixed-income and pension-solutions mandates, largely for UK pension schemes, alongside retirement and insurance businesses.

Ameriprise Financial.text: Minneapolis-based, publicly listed financial-services company spun off from American Express; built around a large network of financial advisors and also owns the asset manager Columbia Threadneedle.

DWS Group.text: Frankfurt-listed asset manager majority-owned by Deutsche Bank, running active, passive (Xtrackers) and alternative strategies for retail and institutional clients in Europe, the Americas and Asia.

Victory Capital.text: San Antonio-based, publicly listed asset manager structured as a holding company for autonomous investment franchises, including the former USAA funds and Pioneer Investments; serves retail and institutional clients.

J.P. Morgan Asset Management.text: New York-based asset-management arm of JPMorgan Chase, running active equity, fixed-income, multi-asset, liquidity and alternative strategies for institutions, intermediaries and individual investors worldwide.

TPG Inc..text: Publicly listed alternative asset manager, founded in San Francisco and Fort Worth, running private equity, growth, impact, real-estate and credit funds for institutional investors worldwide.

Manulife Investment Management.text: Toronto-based asset-management arm of the insurer Manulife (John Hancock in the US), running public-market, private-market and retirement-plan businesses for institutional and retail clients worldwide.

AP Pension.text: Danish pension and life-insurance company, based in Copenhagen, providing occupational and individual pensions; owned by its customers through the association Foreningen AP Pension.

Colonial First State.text: Sydney-based Australian superannuation and investment platform provider, formerly part of Commonwealth Bank and now majority-owned by KKR, serving retail members and financial advisers.

Liontrust Asset Management.text: London-listed independent fund manager organized around autonomous investment teams, running active equity, fixed-income, multi-asset and sustainable strategies, mainly for UK retail investors, financial advisers and institutions.

Azimut Holding.text: Milan-listed independent asset-management and financial-advisory group, partly owned by its own managers and advisers, serving retail clients through a network of financial advisers in Italy and abroad.

Ilmarinen.text: Finnish mutual earnings-related pension insurance company, based in Helsinki, that manages statutory pension cover for private-sector employers and self-employed workers; owned by its customers.

ADIA (Abu Dhabi Investment Authority).text: Sovereign wealth fund owned by the Government of Abu Dhabi, investing the emirate's surplus oil revenues for the long term across global public and private markets.

Investcorp.text: Bahrain-based alternative investment firm with major offices in New York and London, running private equity, real-estate, credit and absolute-return strategies for Gulf private investors and international institutions.

ExodusPoint Capital Management.text: New York-based multi-strategy hedge fund founded by Michael Gelband, a former Millennium executive, allocating capital across many portfolio-manager teams in fixed income, macro and equities.

Lynx Asset Management.text: Stockholm-based systematic hedge-fund manager running trend-following and other model-driven futures strategies (the Lynx program) for institutional investors; part of the Brummer & Partners group.

Sumitomo Mitsui DS Asset Management.text: Tokyo-based asset manager, majority-owned by Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group with Daiwa Securities Group as a major shareholder, running investment trusts and institutional mandates for Japanese and overseas investors.

Daiwa Asset Management.text: Tokyo-based asset manager wholly owned by Daiwa Securities Group, running publicly offered investment trusts (including ETFs) and institutional mandates, mainly for Japanese investors.

Nissay Asset Management.text: Tokyo-based asset-management subsidiary of Nippon Life Insurance (Nissay), one of Japan's major life insurers, running investment trusts and institutional mandates for Japanese pension funds, institutions and retail investors.

E Fund Management.text: Guangzhou-based mutual-fund manager, among mainland China's largest, running public funds, ETFs, pension products and institutional mandates for Chinese retail and institutional investors.

China Europe Fund Management.text: Shanghai-based mutual-fund manager, originally a Sino-European joint venture and among the first mainland fund houses with significant employee ownership; runs public funds for Chinese retail and institutional investors.

China Merchants Fund Management.text: Shenzhen-based mutual-fund manager owned by China Merchants Bank and China Merchants Securities, running public funds, ETFs and institutional mandates for Chinese retail and institutional investors.

Guotai Fund Management.text: Shanghai-based mutual-fund manager, one of the first fund companies licensed in mainland China, running public funds, ETFs and institutional mandates for Chinese investors.

China Universal Asset Management.text: Shanghai-based mutual-fund manager, part-owned by Orient Securities, running public funds, pension products and institutional mandates for Chinese retail and institutional investors.

Maxwealth Fund Management.text: Mainland Chinese mutual-fund manager, majority-owned by Bank of Ningbo, running public funds and institutional mandates for Chinese retail and institutional investors.

China Asset Management (ChinaAMC).text: Beijing-based mutual-fund manager, among mainland China's largest and earliest, majority-owned by CITIC Securities; runs public funds, ETFs, pension products and institutional mandates for Chinese and overseas investors.

Harvest Fund Management.text: Beijing-based mutual-fund manager, one of mainland China's first ten fund houses, with DWS as a long-standing foreign shareholder; runs public funds and institutional mandates for Chinese investors.

Fullgoal Fund Management.text: Shanghai-based mutual-fund manager, one of mainland China's first ten fund houses, part-owned by Bank of Montreal; runs public funds, ETFs and institutional mandates for Chinese investors.

Bosera Asset Management.text: Shenzhen-based mutual-fund manager, one of mainland China's first ten fund houses, with China Merchants Securities as its largest shareholder; runs public funds, ETFs and institutional mandates for Chinese investors.

Tianhong Asset Management.text: Tianjin-registered mutual-fund manager majority-owned by Ant Group; manages Yu'e Bao, the money-market fund embedded in Alipay, alongside index and other public funds, mainly for retail investors.

Ping An Fund Management.text: Shenzhen-based mutual-fund manager controlled by the Ping An Insurance group, running public funds and institutional mandates for Chinese retail and institutional investors.

Dacheng Fund Management.text: Shenzhen-based mutual-fund manager, one of mainland China's first ten fund houses, running public funds and institutional mandates for Chinese retail and institutional investors.

Penghua Fund Management.text: Shenzhen-based mutual-fund manager, one of mainland China's first ten fund houses, owned mainly by Guosen Securities and Intesa Sanpaolo's Eurizon; runs public funds and institutional mandates for Chinese investors.

Korea Teachers Pension.text: South Korean public pension fund for teachers and staff of private schools, operating under the Ministry of Education; invests contributions across domestic and overseas public and private markets.

Invesco Great Wall Fund Management.text: Shenzhen-based mutual-fund manager, a joint venture between Invesco and Great Wall Securities, running public funds and institutional mandates for Chinese retail and institutional investors.

ICBC Credit Suisse Fund Management.text: Beijing-based mutual-fund manager majority-owned by Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, originally formed with Credit Suisse as minority partner; runs public funds and institutional mandates for Chinese investors.

XTX Markets.text: London-based algorithmic trading firm and electronic market maker founded by Alexander Gerko, providing liquidity in equities, fixed income, currencies and commodities to institutional counterparties worldwide.

Hudson River Trading.text: New York-based proprietary trading firm using automated, quantitative strategies to trade its own capital across equities, futures, options, currencies and fixed income on markets worldwide.

Jane Street.text: New York-based proprietary trading firm and market maker, trading its own capital across ETFs, equities, bonds, options and other instruments on exchanges worldwide; builds its systems in OCaml.

Flow Traders.text: Amsterdam-based, Euronext-listed proprietary trading firm and market maker, specializing in ETFs and other exchange-traded products, trading its own capital across global markets.

Optiver.text: Amsterdam-based proprietary trading firm and market maker, privately held, trading its own capital in options, equities, futures, ETFs and other instruments on exchanges worldwide.

Quilter.text: London-listed UK wealth manager, formerly Old Mutual Wealth, combining a financial-advice network, an investment platform and the discretionary manager Quilter Cheviot for UK retail clients and their advisers.

Pictet Asset Management.text: Geneva-based institutional asset-management arm of the Pictet Group, a partner-owned Swiss private bank, running active equity, fixed-income, multi-asset and alternative strategies for institutions and fund investors worldwide.

High-Flyer (幻方量化).text: Hangzhou-based quantitative hedge fund founded by Liang Wenfeng, running systematic strategies in mainland Chinese equities and futures as a private fund for qualified domestic investors.

KB Asset Management.text: Seoul-based asset-management subsidiary of KB Financial Group, one of South Korea's largest banking groups, running public funds, ETFs and institutional mandates for Korean retail and institutional investors.

Elo (Työeläkeyhtiö Elo).text: Finnish mutual pension insurance company, based in Espoo and formed by merging LocalTapiola Pension and Pension Fennia, providing statutory earnings-related pension cover for private-sector employers, employees and the self-employed.

KLP (Kommunal Landspensjonskasse).text: Oslo-based mutual life-insurance company providing occupational pensions for Norway's municipalities, county authorities and health enterprises; owned by its public-sector customers, with an in-house asset-management arm, KLP Kapitalforvaltning.

GitLab Foundation.text: Private grantmaking foundation founded by GitLab co-founder Sid Sijbrandij and endowed with GitLab Inc. stock; funds programs and research aimed at raising people's lifetime earnings and economic mobility.

Aware Super.text: Sydney-based profit-to-member superannuation fund, formerly First State Super, with a membership rooted in New South Wales public-sector, health and education workplaces; open to all Australians.

AustralianSuper.text: Melbourne-based profit-to-member industry superannuation fund, Australia's largest, open to all workers and jointly owned by the ACTU and the Australian Industry Group; invests globally across public and private markets.

Blackstone.text: New York-based, publicly listed alternative asset manager, the world's largest, running private equity, real estate, credit and hedge-fund-solutions businesses for institutional and individual investors worldwide.

PSP Investments.text: Canadian Crown corporation, based mainly in Montreal, that invests the pension contributions of the federal public service, Canadian Forces, RCMP and Reserve Force across public and private markets.

Partners Group.text: Swiss private-markets manager, listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange and headquartered in Baar-Zug, running private equity, credit, infrastructure and real-estate programs for institutional investors and private-wealth clients worldwide.

Hamilton Lane.text: US-listed private-markets investment firm advising and managing capital for institutional and private-wealth investors across primaries, secondaries and direct investments; headquartered in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania.

Houston Endowment.text: Private philanthropic foundation established in 1937 by Jesse H. and Mary Gibbs Jones, funding civic, arts and community work in greater Houston from an endowment it manages.

BNP Paribas Asset Management.text: The asset-management arm of French banking group BNP Paribas, managing institutional, wholesale and retail assets globally; absorbed AXA Investment Managers in 2025.

Capital Group.text: Privately held Los Angeles-based active manager, home of the American Funds, running mutual funds and institutional mandates for retail and institutional investors worldwide.

CDPQ (Caisse de dépôt et placement du Qu.text: Québec's public pension and insurance-plan investor, managing provincial depositors' assets such as the Québec Pension Plan across public and private markets worldwide; trades as La Caisse.

IMCO (Investment Management Corporation.text: Ontario public-sector investment manager created in 2016, pooling and investing the assets of provincial public-sector pension plans and other public bodies from Toronto.

Neuberger.text: Employee-owned New York investment manager offering equity, fixed-income, private-markets and hedge-fund strategies to institutions, advisers and individuals worldwide.

Gates Foundation.text: Seattle-based private foundation funding global health, development and US education; its endowment sits in a separate trust managed outside the foundation's grantmaking organisation.

KKR.text: New York-based global alternative-asset manager investing across private equity, credit, infrastructure and real estate for institutional and individual investors; listed on the NYSE.

Morgan Stanley Investment Management.text: The asset-management division of Morgan Stanley, spanning active equity, fixed income, alternatives and Parametric's customised strategies for institutional and wealth clients worldwide.

Tokio Marine Asset Management.text: Tokyo-based asset manager within the Tokio Marine insurance group, running investment trusts and discretionary mandates for Japanese institutional and retail investors.

USS (Universities Superannuation Scheme).text: The UK's largest private pension scheme by assets, providing pensions for university and higher-education staff; its investments are run in-house by USS Investment Management.

Amova Asset Management (formerly Nikko A.text: Tokyo-headquartered asset manager formerly known as Nikko Asset Management, part of the Sumitomo Mitsui Trust group, managing investment trusts and institutional mandates across Asia and beyond.

Nest (National Employment Savings Trust).text: UK workplace pension scheme set up by the government for automatic enrolment and run by the public corporation Nest Corporation, serving millions of members mainly through default funds.

Northern Trust Asset Management.text: The investment-management arm of Chicago-based Northern Trust Corporation, offering index, quantitative and active strategies to institutions and intermediaries worldwide.

Nuveen.text: Investment manager owned by TIAA, managing fixed income, real estate, equities and alternatives for institutions and individuals; headquartered in New York.

Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan.text: Toronto-based pension plan administering and investing the retirement assets of Ontario's active and retired teachers, with global public- and private-market investments.

UTIMCO.text: Non-profit investment company managing the endowment and operating funds of the University of Texas and Texas A&M University systems, including the Permanent University Fund; based in Austin.

Texas Teacher Retirement System.text: Public pension fund providing retirement and related benefits to Texas public-education employees; Austin-based, with a large internal investment division across public and private markets.

Wellcome Trust.text: London-based charitable foundation funding health research worldwide, financed by an investment portfolio managed in-house by its own investment team.

The Carlyle Group.text: Washington DC-based global alternative-asset manager investing across private equity, credit and investment solutions for institutional and private investors; listed on Nasdaq.
